title: api-gateway: stabilize streaming proxy buffers and adjust routing/payload limits for OpenAI compat
author: Maya Chen
description: Background: We observed a regression in streaming reliability and occasional truncated tool/function-calling payloads after the proxy buffering change in Q4. This manifested as partial JSON payloads on function/tool call boundaries and increased stream latency for long responses. Motivation: Improve streaming stability for hosted API customers, ensure OpenAI compatibility behavior for function/tool calls, and tighten routing rules to avoid oversized payloads being proxied through low-latency routes. Summary of changes: 1) Increase streaming proxy write buffer hysteresis and switch to drain-first flush on connection close to reduce mid-response truncation. 2) Add explicit per-route payload soft-limit checks in the gateway router with a configurable action (reject | chunked-proxy | route-to-batch). Default action is chunked-proxy for known OpenAI-compat routes. 3) Adjust OpenAI-compat layer to emit complete function call JSON only after final chunk flush to prevent partial tool payloads being delivered to SDKs. 4) Add metric instrumentation for buffer backpressure, chunk flush latency, and route rejections. 5) Add integration tests that simulate long streaming responses with function calls and validate end-to-end integrity. Rollout: feature flagged behind rollout/api-gateway-streaming-stability and gated for Dedicated/Private customers for 2 weeks before full rollout. Backwards compatibility: default behavior preserves existing routing but strengthens safety for oversized payloads to avoid silent truncation. Related: linear/ENG-1981, linear/ENG-2043, and incident/INT-412.
commits: increase-proxy-buffer-hysteresis-and-drain-first-flush: adjust write buffer thresholds and implement drain-first close behavior
router: add per-route payload soft-limit and config for oversized actions; default chunked-proxy for /v1/compat routes
openai-compat: delay function-call-emission until final-chunk-flush to ensure complete JSON
tests: add integration test for streaming function calls and payload integrity with mocked slow backend

release_notes: - Improve streaming stability: drain-first flush to reduce response truncation. - Add per-route payload soft-limits with configurable actions to avoid oversized payloads from passing through low-latency routes. - Ensure OpenAI-compat function/tool calls are emitted only after final chunk flush to prevent partial payload delivery. - Added instrumentation for buffer backpressure and flush latency.
